svg.text: FORMAT LINEAGE: Anthropic, Claude Code best practices (Apr 2025)
The Claude Code Loop That Ships: Explore → Plan → Code → Commit (with the exact words to type)
From Anthropic's own best-practices guide. The single biggest lever: give the agent a way to verify its work (tests, screenshots) before it commits.
Read src/auth/ and tests/test_auth.py. Do NOT
write code yet. Summarize how token refresh works
Loading the right files first keeps the plan
grounded in your code, not in guesses.
think hard: propose a plan to fix the refresh
race. List files to change, the failing test to
add first, and risks. Wait for my OK.
Implement the approved plan. Add the failing test
first, make it pass, run the full suite, and show
Tests give the agent a target it can verify itself —
Commit with a message explaining the root cause,
open a PR, and update CLAUDE.md with the new 'run
Documentation written at commit time keeps the next
THINKING BUDGET DIAL (THE KEYWORDS ARE LITERAL)
Each phrase maps to a larger reasoning budget in Claude Code; use the big ones for planning, not for routine edits.
CLAUDE.md CHECKLIST (WHAT THE GUIDE SAYS TO PUT IN IT)
Repository etiquette (branch names, merge vs rebase)
Keep it short; refine it like a prompt
Write tests → commit → code → iterate → commit
Tell it explicitly: 'we are doing TDD, do not write implementation
yet'. Then let it loop against the tests — this is where agents shine.
claude "Write tests for the refresh race based on these cases;
don't implement yet. Confirm they fail."
Give it a way to see results (Puppeteer MCP, iOS simulator, or pasted
screenshots). Output quality jumps after 2-3 visual iterations.
claude "Implement this mock (pasted). Take a screenshot with the
Puppeteer tool and iterate until it matches."
Automate with -p; parallelize with git worktrees
Headless mode runs in CI (issue triage, lint). Separate git worktrees
let several Claude sessions work on independent tasks without stepping
claude -p "Triage this issue and label it" --output-format stream-
Never let it code first. Explore (read-only) → Plan (think hard) → Code against the plan → Commit with a PR description. Verification beats cleverness.
Curated by Nitin Aggarwal • Google Cloud ADK + OpenHands Factory • Proprietary + Confidential
